idiom_name: explicit &SecurityContext parameter or typed request extension (Extension<Principal>); task_local!/thread_local! only for deep guards
implementation_notes: Rust's standard library has no ambient context and references make explicit passing cheap, so the default realization is a &SecurityContext threaded through the layers, or a typed request extension extracted by the handler (axum's Extension<Principal> or a custom extractor over http::request::Extensions) that the middleware populates once at the boundary. Where a guard sits too deep for a parameter - an internal callback, a helper with no access to the request - tokio::task_local! declares a task-scoped LocalKey whose value is readable only inside LocalKey::scope and is not inherited by tasks started with tokio::spawn, and std::thread_local! provides the same for blocking threads with the documented constraint that only shared references to the inner data may be obtained (hence Cell/RefCell for mutability). The classic container plus holder is thereby replaced by the explicit parameter, with the task-local as a deliberate escape hatch rather than the default.
pitfalls: tokio::task_local! values are visible only inside LocalKey::scope and are not inherited by tokio::spawn: a spawned task that reads the key must be given the context explicitly, or the guard sees no binding.
thread_local! data cannot be borrowed across .await in a Send future; snapshot what you need before awaiting, and use Cell/RefCell because only shared references to the inner data are available.
A request extension is typed and consumed by value: an extractor that silently falls back to an anonymous principal turns a missing middleware into an authorization bypass.
